title: Control plane keepalive queue saturation during private VPC upgrade — postmortem & mitigation plan
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: During a staged kernel and dataplane upgrade to private orchestrator agents deployed in customer VPCs, control-plane keepalive traffic from agents was successfully transmitted but dropped or delayed by a new netfilter/eBPF offload path. This resulted in agent-to-controlplane disconnects, controller perception of agent churn, and partial failover triggering connection storms that exhausted NAT and socket resources on customer gateways. Impact window ~45 minutes; affected 3 customer clusters running Dedicated/Private pilot configurations. This ticket captures the postmortem analysis, immediate mitigations, and concrete follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary:
- Customer impact: 3 private deployments experienced degraded API routing and control plane commands failed for ~45 minutes. Surface-level symptoms: increased control-plane error rates, orchestrator leader thrashing, elevated NAT port usage on customer edge routers.
- Scope: small number of Private deployments running kernel 6.4 with vendor eBPF offload. No hosted customers affected.
- Customer impact severity: high (brief outage of control-plane dependent operations)
timeline: 2026-03-05 02:10 UTC: Staged kernel+eBPF dataplane rollout begins for private agent image revision v2.11 (orchestrator-managed).
2026-03-05 02:38 UTC: First cluster reports agent heartbeat gaps; operator notes spike in control-plane connection resets on console.
2026-03-05 02:45 UTC: Automated canary rollback not triggered due to false-negative health signal (agents reported local service up).
2026-03-05 02:50 UTC: Multiple clusters display leader election churn and increase in control-plane request latency. Oncall paged.
2026-03-05 03:05 UTC: Engineers trace to large socket queue / netfilter drop counters on customer gateways; NAT port exhaustion symptoms observed.
2026-03-05 03:20 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: reduce agent keepalive frequency and widen keepalive timeouts via remote-config; restart of edge agent proxies to flush conntrack.
2026-03-05 03:40 UTC: Agent connectivity stabilizes; rollout halted pending root cause analysis.
root_cause: A change in the agent datapath (vendor kernel 6.4 + eBPF offload) altered packet steering such that control-plane keepalive SYN/ACK and short TCP probes were being redirected into an accelerated path that bypassed the connection tracking expectations used by our proxy. The accelerated path had more aggressive per-CPU queue thresholds and drop-on-full behavior. During the rollout, keepalive bursts from many agents coincided with a slightly smaller conntrack table limit on customer gateways, producing packet drops at the edge. The orchestration layer misinterpreted transient agent-side liveness as service failure (false-negative health checks) and attempted leader elections and reconnections, amplifying traffic and causing NAT port pressure. Contributing factors: (1) insufficient pre-rollout testing against vendor kernel+eBPF offload path, (2) conservative keepalive tuning with low headroom for queuing/drops, (3) automated canary health checks relying on local agent metrics rather than end-to-end control-plane acknowledgement.
action_items: A1: Add a vendor-kernel compatibility test harness exercising eBPF offload paths with simulated conntrack pressure. Owner: Rafael Ortiz. Estimate: 4. Due: 2026-03-20.

A2: Update agent health checks to include end-to-end control-plane ack (round-trip) metric so canary rollbacks trigger on control-plane observed failures. Owner: Priya Nair. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-15.

A3: Increase default conntrack and socket headroom toggles in the private-agent bootstrap with opt-out for constrained gateways; document in runbook. Owner: Diego Morales. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-14.
A4: Implement exponential jitter on keepalive bursts and add rate limiting for reconnection storms at the client side. Owner: Rafael Ortiz. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-03-22.

A5: Create a pre-deployment checklist for private kernel/datapath upgrades that includes synthetic canary testing against customers with representative edge topologies. Owner: SRE team (lead: Hannah Lee). Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-18.

A6: Ship a control-plane & private-agent dashboard panel showing conntrack utilization, NAT port usage, and eBPF queue drop counters as first-class graphs for faster triage. Owner: Observability team (lead: Marcus Chen). Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-03-28.

A7: Update rollback heuristic: if more than 3% of agents in a cohort show control-plane RTT > 3x baseline within 5 minutes, automatically pause rollout and notify oncall. Owner: Release Engineering. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-16.
mitigations_applied: - Reduced agent keepalive frequency from 15s to 60s for impacted clusters to break burst patterns (temporary remote-config).
- Flushed conntrack entries and restarted edge proxy on affected clusters (manual).
- Rollout paused across remaining private clusters.
postmortem_notes: Decisions made: prioritize agent-side backpressure and jitter over immediate tuning server-side values in customer environments. Trade-offs: longer keepalive means slower failure detection for true agent failures (accepted temporarily) while we implement end-to-end health checks to avoid false positives. We will also engage vendor engineering to confirm eBPF offload semantics and recommended conntrack defaults. Review feedback from PM (J. Patel) asked for clearer customer communication templates; added an outbound incident mail draft to the follow_up_links.
notes_for_post_release_review: Schedule a 45-minute cross-team review with SRE, Release, Observability, and PM to validate mitigations and sign off on rollout checklist. Invite: oncall rotation owners from impacted customers.
